headline: REGIS HAS UNTIL MONDAY TO MATCH GENESIS' $5.6B VAULT BID — 600KOZ/YR AUSTRALIAN GOLD MAJOR AT STAKE (ASX:GMD/VAU/RRL)
snippet: Vault Minerals extended the matching right period for Regis Resources (ASX: RRL) to 11:59pm AWST on Monday July 13, giving Regis additional business days to respond to Genesis Minerals' binding A$5.6 billion proposal — 0.7629 new Genesis shares plus A$0.475 cash per Vault share, a 14.5% premium to the Regis scheme, implying A$5.27/share — that would create an A$12.6 billion Western Australia-dominant gold major with 600,000–700,000 oz/year combined output. Regis must now match, counter, or cede Vault by Monday's close; this is the most significant ASX gold consolidation contest of 2026 and its outcome directly determines which operator controls the Leonora-Laverton district's dominant production profile.

headline: ATHA ENERGY RIB NORTH: 37M WIDEST URANIUM INTERSECTION YET, SECONDARY EAST-WEST STRUCTURE 1KM AWAY — SIXTH ANGILAK DISCOVERY IN 15 MONTHS (TSXV:SASK)
source_name: Investing News Network / ATHA Energy Corp.
snippet: ATHA Energy (TSXV: SASK) reported July 9 that drill hole RIBN-DD-003 at the Rib North Discovery at the Angilak Uranium Project in Nunavut returned the widest uranium intersection to date — 37 metres of composite mineralization — with the first eight holes confirming continuity over more than 300 metres of strike, plus a newly identified secondary east-west mineralised structure approximately 1 km from the main Rib North area displaying identical basement-hosted vein style and albite-hematite alteration. This is a distinct discovery zone from the Lac 50 Northwest result released July 8; ATHA has now produced two separately confirmed uranium discovery-grade results in consecutive days at Angilak, a discovery rate that compresses the typical multi-year exploration timeline to resource definition.

headline: K92 KORA Q2: 46,093 OZ AuEq, RECORD LATERAL DEVELOPMENT — TWO NEW MINING FRONTS FUEL H2 RAMP TO 225,000 OZ GUIDANCE (TSX:KNT)
snippet: K92 Mining (TSX: KNT) reported July 8 that the Kora underground mine in Papua New Guinea delivered 46,093 oz AuEq (42,931 oz Au, 1.78 million lbs Cu, 50,109 oz Ag) in Q2 2026, alongside record quarterly lateral development, ore tonnes mined, total material mined, and ore tonnes processed, with the company maintaining full-year guidance of 190,000–225,000 oz AuEq and explicitly flagging H2 as the stronger half as two new mining fronts complete their development ramp. K92's unbroken streak of record mine physicals while maintaining high-grade gold output in a structurally complex Papua New Guinea underground mine makes it a reference standard for junior-to-mid-tier gold production quality — and at $4,100/oz gold, its operating margins are generating the cash flow that funds further growth without equity dilution.

headline: VANECK GOLD SWOT: K92 HOLDS 50-DAY MA AS MINERS SET UP FOR H2 RECOVERY — PRODUCTION BEATS PRECEDE SECTOR RE-RATINGS | GoldSeek
snippet: VanEck's weekly Gold SWOT column highlights K92 Mining's technical resilience — holding above its 50-day moving average while posting record Q2 mine physicals and reiterating guidance — as a leading indicator that gold equity laggards are beginning to attract value-focused buyers ahead of a potential H2 recovery phase. With gold mining stocks near multi-year valuation lows relative to the metal price, VanEck identifies a setup where strong production guidance reiterations from quality operators historically precede the sector re-ratings that close the gold-to-miner ratio gap; the key condition for acceleration is the July 14 CPI print confirming that Fed rate-hike odds have peaked.

headline: LUNDIN: MINING STOCKS AT HISTORIC DISCOUNT TO GOLD — SILVER AND EQUITIES STILL THE CATCH-UP TRADE THIS BULL MARKET | GoldSeek
snippet: Brien Lundin (Gold Newsletter) argues that the current discount of gold mining equities to the physical metal is one of the most historically anomalous of any gold bull market on record — a direct result of this cycle being propelled by price-insensitive central bank accumulation rather than speculative Western retail flows, which left silver and miners without the momentum needed to close the gold-to-miner ratio in the early stages. Lundin's thesis: the absence of a speculative blow-off in mining stocks through gold's move from $3,000 to $4,000+ means the catch-up trade still lies ahead; at current valuations, mining equities offer leveraged exposure to a gold price that has structural central bank demand support at every meaningful dip.

headline: MACQUARIE: $6.27/LB COPPER IS RUNNING AHEAD OF REALITY — LME STOCKS HIT 8-YEAR HIGH AS 262,000T 2026 SURPLUS LOOMS
snippet: Macquarie argues that copper's recent surge toward $6.27/lb runs materially ahead of physical fundamentals: LME inventories are at eight-year highs, visible stocks have risen 870,000 tonnes since January 2025, and the bank projects a 262,000-tonne refined copper surplus in 2026 — widening to 700,000+ tonnes annually in 2027–2028 — even after accounting for 783,000 tonnes of supply disruptions. Macquarie raised its 2026 average forecast to $13,165/tonne reflecting price momentum, but forecasts a floor at $11,000/tonne ($4.99/lb) by Q3 2027, and is specifically sceptical that AI data centre demand will materialise as quickly as the market assumes due to grid constraints, equipment shortages, and the growing shift to optical connectivity.

headline: GOLD FIRMS TO $4,111, SILVER TO $60.32 AS IRAN RETURNS TO TALKS — JULY 14 CPI IS THE FINAL WALL FOR PRECIOUS METALS
snippet: Gold spot recovered to $4,111/oz on July 10 — up from the $4,087 post-FOMC selloff low of July 9 — as Iran's return to nuclear negotiations eased geopolitical risk and the dollar softened modestly, while silver rebounded to $60.32 (+0.62%) with the dual oil-shock and rate-hike pressure fading from its worst levels. The July 14 CPI print remains the decisive binary event for metals direction: a reading above 4.0% would push September rate-hike probability toward 65% and extend the gold consolidation range, while a sub-3.8% print would compress rate expectations and potentially break the $4,200 ceiling toward the World Gold Council's upside scenario of $4,500+ for H2.

headline: CANTERRA STARTS 8,000M PHASE 2 AT BUCHANS — CANADA'S PREMIER VMS CAMP TARGETS MAIDEN RESOURCE BY Q4 2026 (TSXV:CTM)
snippet: Canterra Minerals (TSXV: CTM) commenced approximately 8,000 metres of Phase 2 diamond drilling in Newfoundland's Buchans copper-zinc district on July 8 — 2,000 metres of infill at the Lundberg anchor deposit and 6,000 metres across satellite VMS targets including Lemarchant, Boomerang, Long Lake, and Tulks — targeting a maiden mineral resource estimate for Lundberg in Q4 2026. The Buchans camp historically produced more than 16 million tonnes of high-grade Cu-Zn-Pb-Ag-Au; Canterra's consolidated land position across five VMS deposits makes it the district's first resource-stage company in decades, and the Q4 maiden resource is the re-rating milestone for what remains one of Canada's most underappreciated historical mining districts.

headline: NORTHWEST COPPER DEPLOYS THREE RIGS AT KWANIKA: 10,000M TO EXPAND 226M LB CU RESOURCE, PEA UPDATE AHEAD (TSXV:NWST)
snippet: NorthWest Copper (TSXV: NWST) announced July 8 that three diamond drill rigs are active at the 100%-owned Kwanika copper-gold project in British Columbia — targeting up to 10,000 metres focused on upgrading the Western Zone underground resource and confirming pit-zone near-surface mineralization — with results expected late summer and a PEA update targeted for mid-2026. The current Kwanika Indicated Resource is 226.6 million lbs Cu, 383,000 oz Au, and 1,035,000 oz Ag at 16.22 million tonnes; the 2026 program is designed to provide resource confidence for a PEA update that will define the project's open-pit versus underground trade-offs at current copper prices — a decision framework that becomes more valuable as copper supply-chain nationalism intensifies the premium on Tier-1 Canadian copper projects.
